claims.text: The initial CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous matrix free of secondary oxide phases.
Controlled oxidation during processing can form uniformly distributed nano-oxide particles within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Embedded nano-oxide particles act as preformed micro-passivators.
Embedded nano-oxide particles provide a lubricious particle–matrix interface.
The nano-oxide particles remain stable within the alloy matrix during tribocorrosion.
After wear removes the protective surface film, embedded oxide particles provide localized sites for immediate oxide reformation.
Localized oxide reformation accelerates repassivation of worn surfaces.
The oxide particles lower wear-induced mechanical damage.
Rapid restoration of a passivating layer mitigates corrosion.
Under moderate loads in 3.5 wt% NaCl, the oxide-containing composite will have lower wear depth than monolithic CoCrFeNi.
Under moderate loads in 3.5 wt% NaCl, the oxide-containing composite will have a lower corrosion rate than monolithic CoCrFeNi.
The composite will synergistically reduce simultaneous wear and corrosion relative to the monolithic alloy.
Very high loads can fracture or debond the embedded oxide particles.
Particle fracture or debonding diminishes the composite's beneficial tribocorrosion effects.
Sub-optimal particle–matrix bonding can cause the proposed mechanism to fail.
The proposed controlled comparison uses an oxide-containing CoCrFeNi composite and a monolithic CoCrFeNi baseline under otherwise matched reciprocating tribocorrosion conditions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both wear and corrosion under moderate loads would falsify the hypothesis.
